script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for November 1. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Sprints are dramatic, but races are won by those who keep going.  Endurance is sustained capacity—the ability to maintain effort when others fade.  Many endeavors are marathons, not sprints.

Endurance requires finding sustainable pace—effort you can maintain. Too fast, you burn out. Too slow, you don't progress. The art is finding the edge of sustainability. Mental fatigue usually precedes physical exhaustion.  Your body can often do more than your mind thinks.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Persistence often matters more than intensity.  What you can sustain determines what you achieve.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Endurance Check - How Long Can You Go?.

Here's your activity: Where does your endurance fail—in work, exercise, relationships, focus? What's your sustainable pace? How could you train your capacity to sustain effort for longer periods? This helps you assess and build sustained capacity.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about going longer without stopping can be applied to endurance check - how long can you go?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
